resources.string: Open sites that block Iran (Gemini, AI tools, developer services) through a DNS provider that proxies them abroad, while Aether keeps opening filtered sites.
The device resolves names through the servers below instead of 1.1.1.1 / 8.8.8.8. Sites the provider covers see the provider\'s country; everything else keeps the WARP exit.
Only applies to the Aether-only chain. With Psiphon or Tor in front, the exit is already abroad and this setting is ignored.
IPv4 addresses, separated by commas, spaces or new lines. Port 53 only (UDP). Up to 8 servers, tried in order.
None of these is a usable server (unicast IPv4, port 53). The default resolvers will be used until one is.

The Smart DNS servers and the proxy addresses below are reached straight from your connection instead of through WARP. Turn on only if your provider accepts registered or Iranian IPs only; that traffic is then visible to your ISP, and Aether\'s own lookups use the normal DNS.

The addresses the provider\'s DNS answers covered sites with (its SNI proxies). A provider that checks your IP checks it there too, so these have to go direct as well. IPv4 or CIDR (/16 or narrower). To find them, resolve a covered site with the provider\'s DNS.
None of these is a usable proxy address (unicast IPv4, or a CIDR of /16 or narrower). Covered sites will still go through WARP.
This device refused a tunnel without IPv6, so IPv6 is still offered to apps in this session. Covered sites may open over IPv6 without the provider\'s proxy and still show the sanctions error.

Android\'s Private DNS (Settings, Network, Private DNS) must be Off or Automatic, otherwise the system ignores these servers. IPv6 is not offered to apps while Smart DNS is on. Check a site the provider covers, not an IP checker, to confirm it works.
